lawyer:
MI Farooqui, with M Salimullah, and Faisal H Khan, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner
Sharifuddin Chakladar, AAG ----- For the Respondents
parties:
Abdur Rouf ----- Petitioner
Vs
Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment: The petitioner is a national of Bangladesh and is in the service of Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation. He migrated from India in 1947 for permanent settlement in the then East Bengal, now Bangladesh. He has been living in Dhaka as a permanent resident with the members of his family. He obtained a Domicile certificate on 26.1.1950 from the District Magistrate, Dhaka. The certificate of Domicile is annexed to the petition and marked as Annexure 'A' The petitioner joined the Pakistan Jute Mills Association on 5.8.1959. His service was confirmed on 3.3.1964. He was transferred to Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation and absorbed as such with effect from 1.6.1973 and his service upto 31.5.1973 with Bangladesh Jute Mills Association was treated as continuous service with the Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation. The true copies of appointment letter dated 5.8.1959, letter dated 27.8.1966 confirming his service Memo dated 31.10.1973 and Memo, dated 29.11.1973 transferring to and obsorbing him in Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation are annexed to the petition and marked as Annexures 'B' B(1), B(2) and B(3) respectively. Since he has been serving in the Corporation drawing all service benefits from time to time, he received such benefits in 1974, 1975, 1976, 1978 and 1979. The copies of such Memoranda are annexed to the petition and marked as Annexures C, C(1) C(2), C(3), C(4), C(5) and C (6) respectively. The petitioner was earlier allowed a house being house No. 7, Lane No.4, Block No. C, Section No. 10, Mirpur Housing Estate under Memo No. 37 54/CHS dated 11.7.1963 by the Assistant Commissioner Works (Housing and Planning) of the Government of the then East Pakistan and a deed of conveyance dated 5.8.1963 leased out to the petitioner by conveyance deed for a period of 99 years measuring 131 sq. yards and transferring the house (one room) built thereon for a consideration of Rs. 2700.00 by hire purchase on payment of balance amount within 15 years and got delivery of possession by two Memoranda, dated 7.8.1963 and 3.9.1963. The true copies of the appointment letter, registered conveyance deed and other Memoranda are annexed to the petition and marked as Annexures D, D(1), D(2) and D(3) respectively. After the liberation of the country on 16th December, 1971 during the abnormal situation' which followed the petitioner was dispossessed from the said property. The petitioner claims that he made several representation to different authorities including Deputy Commissioner, Sub-Divisional Officer, Assistant Commissioner and Secretary, Ministry of Works in April, 1972 and again on 22.2.1975, 21.10.1975 and  5. 8.1976. The Ministry of Works by its Memo dated 3.6.1977 directed the petitioner to produce the documents and papers in support of his claim which he accordingly complied by his letter dated 16.6.1977 but to no effect. Subsequently, on 11.9.1978 the petitioner made another representation to the Ministry of Works for release and restoration of his property. Thereafter on 19.9.1978 the petitioner received a Memo from the Ministry asking him to supply certain information in the prescribed form-A. The petitioner submitted the information as asked for. On 24.3.1982 the Martial Law was declared in the country and the petitioner made representation to the Chief Martial Law Administrator on 28.4.1982 for release and restoration of his property. The petitioner also continued to make representation to the Ministry of Works on 14.6.1984 and 25.12.1984. Thereupon the petitioner received two Memoranda, dated 27.1.1985 and 10.3.1985 from the Ministry asking him to produce documents and papers in support of his claim. The petitioner submitted necessary documents and papers on 31.3.1985 but to his surprise the petitioner again received a memo, dated 21.4.85 asking him to remain present on 6.5.1985 at 11-00 AM before the Deputy Secretary (A-P-1) and accordingly the petitioner appeared in person before the said authority. Then on 14.5.1985 and 5.8.1985 the petitioner made further representation. The petitioner then received a memo dated 14.10.1985 from the Senior Scale Section Officer, Ministry of Works asking the petitioner to produce all original documents and papers in support of his case within seven days. The petitioner complied with the direction. The copies of the applications and memoranda are annexed to the petition and marked as Annexures E series. It is stated by the petitioner that he is a Khan by family title. But he did not write his usual family title, and because his name in some papers appeared with his title 'Khan' it created confusion with regard to his identity and to resolve proper identification the signatures and thumb impression of the petitioner was taken by one Mr. M Shamsul Haque, Senior Scale Section Officer, Ministry of Works on 26.10.1985 on two papers to compare the same with those appearing on the conveyance deed, dated 6.8.1963 (Annexure D-1) in order to obtain opinion from the Finger Print Expert of CID, Bangladesh. The expert, in his opinion, found the specimen of the petitioner to be identical with those appearing on the conveyance deed, dated 6.3.1963. It is stated that the report to that effect was lying with the relevant record of the Govt. While the matter was pending before the Govt. in the Ministry of Works, the Abandoned Building (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No. 54 of 1985) came in to force providing the provision for constitution of the Court of Settlement which also created a right for the persons aggrieved to file fresh claim before the Court against the enlistment of the properties as abandoned property. The petitioner under section 7 (1) of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provisions) Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No. 54 of 1985) filed his claim stating, inter alia, that the property in question does not answer to the description of abandoned property and, in his support, he filed all necessary documents and papers referred to above. The application was restored as case No. 760 of 1987 (Ka-165 Mirpur Dhaka). The Government did not file any written statement against the material facts of the case of the petitioner. In the absence of written statement or objection the case was taken up by the Court of Settlement for hearing on 21.12.1988 in the presence of Mr. Siddique Ahmed Chowdhury, Chairman and Mr. Abdur Rahman Mia, Member who affected themselves as a court of Settlement in violation of section 9 of the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985. It is stated that while they were coram non judice the Government lawyer Syeda Ferdousi Begum objected against the release of the property on the verbal submissions that the petitioner was original lessee of the Government as the petitioner's name was Abdur Rouf Khan and also submitted that the original lessee who was Abdur Rouf had left for Pakistan and the petitioner was an imposter" and had no locus standi to file the case, When the petitioner found that his very locus standi was under challenge he instantly filed two applications, one with a prayer for a direction upon the Govt. respondent to file written statement in order to fix up the liability of wrong submission with regard to identification and to allow the petitioner to examine the Government record to verify the filing of the expert. By another application, the petitioner informed the Chairman and the Member that the Government in the Ministry of Works had got verified the petitioner's signature and thumb impression for his identification and without disposing of the said two applications instantly Mr. Siddique Ahmed Chowdhury, Chairman and Mr. Abdur Rahman Mia, Member kept the same in record fixing on 24.12.1988 for hearing of the case before the Full Court i.e. when the Court would be properly constituted on 24.12.1988. The Court of Settlement was properly constituted with Mr. Siddique Ahmed Chowdhury as Chairman, Mr. Jalal Ahmed and Mr. Abdur Rahman Mia as Members and the case was taken up for hearing and to meet the point of locus standi of the petitioner, the petitioner pressed for disposal of the aforesaid two applications (Annexure G and G(1) to resolve the dispute about the identification of the petitioner under challenge. The Court of Settlement declined to take up the two petitions for hearing on the grounds that the onus was on the petitioner to prove his case without resort to any document or finding in the Government record or file. It is alleged that the Court of Settlement without examining the Government record and documents and papers filed by the petitioner, dismissed the case on the allegation of non-prosecution without giving any finding on merit. The judgment and order dated 24.12.88 impugned by the petitioner is annexed to the petition and marked as Annexure A-1.
